question.leadin: Answer the following about people in the "Leaders" section of the 2017 TIME 100.
question.text: This man won the 2016 Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to make peace with rebel groups in Colombia, including FARC.

swap.text: On June 15, 1813, Bol´ıvar issued a Decree proclaiming this violent end against the Spanish in South America. This decree guaranteed no harm would come to anyone who murdered a Spaniard or had previously done so.
swap.answerHtml: Decree of War to the Death (accept Decreto de Guerra a Muerte)
swap.answer: Decree of War to the Death
swap.clue: During the Admirable Campaign, Bolivar issued this Decree as a response to Spanish massacres. This order permitted murder of Spanish born citizens opposing independence.

question.leadin: Answer the following about British prime minister Margaret Thatcher and education.
question.text: Schoolteacher Diana Gould pressed Thatcher on the sinking of this country's ship General Belgrano during the Falklands War, which was fought between the UK and this country. Earlier, this country was led by Juan Peron.
question.clue: This country gained independence during the May Revolution, as commemorated by a square in its capital city.

swap.leadin: During a coup, this leader committed suicide by AK-47 at the Palacio de La Moneda.
swap.text: Name this socialist leader, who was replaced by the far-right dictator Augusto Pinochet as a result of that coup.
swap.clue: This leader "Had to Die" according to an essay by Gabriel Garcia Marquez, and he likely died holding a sub-machine gun gifted to him by Fidel Castro.

question.text: The head of Pinochet's DINA secret police, Manuel Contreras, was the mastermind of this program of CIA- backed state terrorism in South America. Jorge Videla led the Dirty War in Argentina as part of this initiative.
question.clue: A man involved in this campaign was accused of genocide against the Ache people, and another man involved in this campaign .

swap.leadin: According to a wild rumor, Emil Holmdahl stole this man's skull and sold it to a wealthy American who may have been the father of George H.W. Bush.
swap.text: Name this revolutionary, whose 1923 assassination was likely carried out on the orders of Alvaro Obregon. John Pershing failed to capture this revolutionary in the wake of his raid on the southwestern town of Columbus.
swap.answerHtml: Pancho Villa [or Francisco Villa or José Doroteo Arango Arámbula]
swap.clue: This man's capture of Ojinaga was delayed because the cameramen filming the battle had to move into position first.

question.text: This war between Chile, Peru, and Bolivia was fought over a resource-rich section of the Atacama Desert, but is more commonly referred to by ocean it was largely fought in. Bolivia has been landlocked ever since.
question.clue: At this war's Battle of Iquique, the Esmeralda was sunk by the Huascar, which was later captured at the Battle of Angamos.

swap.text: This Dominican dictator ordered the massacre on the pretext of protecting the Haitian-Dominican border. He had Columbia professor Jesus Galindez abducted in New York City as part of a brazen regime of state terrorism.
swap.answerHtml: Rafael Trujillo [or Rafael Leónidas Trujillo Molina; accept El Jefe or The Chief]
swap.clue: This dictator took power by overthrowing Horacio Vasquez, used pancake makeup to make himself appear whiter, and unsuccessfully attempted to blow up Venezuelan president Romulo Betancourt.

question.leadin: Literacy tests in this country meant that most of its Black population was ineligible to vote in postwar elections.
question.text: Name this country where a civil rights agenda was promoted in the 1960s by a politician nicknamed Jango, who served as a vice president under Juscelino Kubitschek ("zhoo-seh-LEE-noo koo-bee-SHEK").
question.answerHtml: Brazil [or Federative Republic of Brazil or República Federativa do Brasil]
question.clue: Princess Isabel, on behalf of Emperor Pedro II, signed this country's 1888 Golden Law, making it the last Western country to ban slavery.

swap.text: As Haiti's ruler from 1957 to 1971, he organized the Tontons Macoutes secret police and institutionalized the nationalistic doctrine of the Groupe des Griots.
swap.clue: Clement Barbot served in this man's stead while he was comatose for nine hours.

question.text: This structure on the Parana River is shared between Paraguay and Brazil. This second largest hydroelectric facility in the world in terms of generation lies north of the friendship bridge connecting Ciudad del Este and Foz do Iguacu.
question.clue: Operation Mymba Kuera saved animals from the area flooded by this dam which submerged Guaira Falls and provides roughly 25% of Brazil's electricity.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about influential historians.
swap.text: This Spanish monk engaged in the Valladolid Debate with Juan Gines de Sepulveda, arguing that the American Indians deserved the same human rights that Europeans had. He outlined the cruelties of the Spaniards in his A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies.
swap.clue: Protestant apologists drew on this man's work to create the "Black Legend."

question.leadin: Charles Leclerc offered to make peace with this leader, only to capture him and ship him off to France.
question.text: Name this patriot, a Haitian Revolutionary who led the slave revolt which took control of what was then Saint- Dominigue and laid the foundation for modern Haiti.
question.clue: This man is quoted as saying "In overthrowing me, you have cut down only the tree trunk of liberty" upon his arrest in 1802 by Jean-Baptiste Brunet.

swap.text: The PRI's poor handling of the earthquake was one of the reasons that led Cuauhtemoc ("kwa-ooh-tay-mok"), a member of this family, to run against it as part of the PRD. An earlier president of Mexico with this surname nationalized the country's oil industry to create Pemex.
swap.clue: This surname of a PRD candidate for president. Another politician with this surname exiled Plutarco Elias Calles ("ploo-TARK-oh eh-LEE-as kai-EZ").

question.leadin: The brutal methods promoted by this man resulted in rural militias called rondas allying with the military against his militants.
question.text: Name this man, who was captured in 1992 after a house in Lima was searched after DIRCOTE operatives noticed too much garbage being taken out of a supposedly one-person house.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Plutarco Elias Calles.
swap.text: This term is applied to the period of Plutarco Calles' utter dominance as the chief of the PNR and Mexican politics from 1928 to 1935, even though he was no longer in office.
swap.clue: The founder of the PRI, Plutarco Calles, served as the de facto leader of Mexico during this 1928 to 1934 period which refers to a popular sobriquet for Calles.

question.leadin: This woman's press freedom foundation is led by her daughter Cristina, who was put under house arrest in 2021 and banned from running for office.
question.text: Name this woman who ran the opposition newspaper La Prensa after her husband Pedro was assassinated by the Somoza regime. She was later elected President of Nicaragua in 1990.
question.clue: Anger at the Somozas grew thanks to reporting by La Prensa, which this person edited after her husband was murdered in 1978. This politician beat Daniel Ortega in 1990 to become Nicaragua's first female president.

swap.leadin: This man was deposed with CIA help after trying to expropriate lands held by the United Fruit Company.
swap.text: Identify this man who was part of an officer revolt against Jorge Ubico and succeeded Juan Jose Arevalo as president of his nation.
swap.clue: In 1954, Rios Montt participated in the CIA Operation PBSUCCESS, which overthrew this president who redistributed land from huge estates to peasants in Decree 900.

question.leadin: Identify these scandals of the Grant administration, FTPE.
question.text: Joseph Fry was accused of using this ship to carry contraband to the Cubans during the 10 year war; this lead to several executions and straining of diplomatic relations with Spain.
question.clue: In 1873, Joseph Fry and 52 other crew and passengers were executed as pirates after this ship was captured by the Spanish, causing a strain in Spanish-American relations. This ship had been carrying arms to rebelling Cubans while flying the American flag.

swap.leadin: This man made the leader of the CROM labor union, Luis Morones, a secretary of labor and commerce but later split with Morones.
swap.text: Name this man who had de facto power during a period called the maximato. He promoted a grand literacy agenda and possibly orchestrated the assassination of Venustiano Carranza with his predecessor, Alvaro Obregon.
swap.clue: His inveterate enemy during his presidency was Anacleto Gonzalez Flores, a leader of the National League for the Defense of Religious Freedom.
